text:
The mistake almost every Kamakura day-tripper makes: starting at the big shrine by the station, then racing to the Great Buddha before it closes. Flip it, and you get both without the rush 👇

👀 One opening time on this list surprised even us. Spot it here 👉 https://japanbystation.com/kamakura-from-noon-temples-or-sunset

❌ THE USUAL ORDER

Tsurugaoka Hachimangu first, because it's 10 minutes from Kamakura Station. Then lunch, a slow walk down the shopping street, and suddenly it's 16:00 and Hase's temples are about to stop letting people in.

✅ THE BETTER ORDER

Go straight to Hase on the Enoden. The Great Buddha takes last entry at 16:45 from October to March, and Hasedera at 16:30. Do those while they're open.

🌅 THE PAYOFF

Hachimangu's gates are open from 6:00 to 20:00 every day of the year, and entry is free. So you can walk up its main steps after sunset, when most of the afternoon crowd is already on the train home.

📌 SAVE THIS ORDER

Hase temples → sunset at Inamuragasaki → Hachimangu → dinner near the station. Three short Enoden rides: ¥200, ¥200 and ¥220.

It's a small change, but it turns a rushed afternoon into a relaxed one.
